prompt:
Wide editorial illustration of a creative technology team, all working simultaneously and independently in a warm open studio workspace. 16:9 panoramic format. Painterly brushwork, visible texture — reads as a thoughtful commissioned magazine illustration, not a photo, not flat-design, not animation.

COMPOSITION:
A long shared desk and surrounding stations stretch across the full width of the frame. Six people are spread across this space, each completely absorbed in their own work. No one is looking at anyone else. No one is waiting. The overall feeling is: six lanes of motion, all running at full speed at the same moment.

THE PEOPLE (left to right across the frame):

1. Far left — Ethan (security): a white man, late thirties, short dark hair, subtle beard-stubble, dark zip-collar jacket. Seated at the far left, facing dual monitors that cast a cool green-tinted glow on his face (suggesting terminal / code). His expression is watchful, controlled. The corner he occupies is slightly darker than the rest of the room.

2. Center-left — Indy (researcher): a white man in his mid-forties, wavy medium-length light brown hair with some grey, green henley shirt. Seated to Claude's left, leaning forward toward a laptop screen. His desk has colorful sticky notes, a large ceramic mug, and a small stack of open books. His expression is intent — tracking something, mid-thought.

3. CENTER (focal anchor) — The director: a Black man in his forties, close-cropped hair, navy cardigan over a light collared shirt. Seated at center of the long shared desk, body turned slightly toward the viewer, gaze down on an open notebook filled with flowing connection diagrams — arrows linking nodes — the sketch of a system being built. Calm, fully absorbed. A few stacked books behind him on a low shelf. Warm lamp to his right.

4. Center-right — Devin (developer): a white man in his early thirties, short dark hair, relaxed navy t-shirt. Standing at a desk to Claude's right, facing a large code-editor monitor (blue-tinted screen glow, abstract lines of color suggesting code — not legible). One hand rests on a wireless keyboard. A small leafy houseplant sits at the corner of his desk. Focused expression.

5. Right — Casey (writer): a white woman, early thirties, shoulder-length auburn hair, rust-coral top. Seated further right, at a warm wooden writing desk with a large open notebook in front of her. Pen in hand, leaning slightly forward. A dark ceramic coffee mug to one side. Morning or late-afternoon light falls across her shoulder from a window at the far right.

6. Far right — Maya (designer): an Asian woman, black blunt-cut bob, black turtleneck sweater. Seated at the far right of the scene at a large design monitor (muted screen glow). Right hand rests on a drawing tablet stylus. A pinboard or wall behind her has abstract color-swatch fragments — no legible text.

LIGHTING AND COLOR:
Primary light source: warm incandescent overhead (amber, honey-yellow). Secondary lights: the individual screen glows — cool green-tinted at far left (Ethan), blue-white center-right (Devin), muted neutral for the designer (Maya). Late afternoon window light enters from the far right, backlighting Casey slightly. The palette is warm earth tones — amber, tan, muted navy, olive — with those three cool screen accents as counterpoint. No single dominant color; the warmth unifies.

MOOD:
Not a posed group portrait. This is a documentary-style illustration of a team mid-sprint. Ambient, lived-in, real. The energy is focused and quiet — the hum of work, not the performance of it.

Non-negotiable constraints:
- ZERO readable text anywhere — no legible characters on screens, notebooks, books, sticky notes, posters, or any surface. Screen content must be abstract: blobs of color, geometric shapes, or smeared light suggesting code / design / research without forming letters or numbers.
- Anatomy must be plausible: correct number of limbs per person, no fused or extra fingers, no partial bodies clipping through desks or walls, faces have all features.
- Physics must be coherent: people are seated or standing at their workstations naturally, objects rest on surfaces, no floating items.
- The scene fills the full 16:9 canvas edge to edge — no dead white or gray margins. Intentional negative space (open air above figures, window light at edges) is fine; blank borders are not.
- No explicit real-world brand logos or watermarks.
- Each person's screen must face the person using it, not the viewer; we see the backs or edges of monitors, not the display surfaces.
- Editorial illustration style: painterly brushwork, visible texture, NOT flat-vector, NOT photorealistic, NOT Pixar / animated.
